recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. It completes the seed issue's concrete authored/authored-on/authoredon compatibility case without changing normative primary search codes. Handle any broader preferred-code inventory as separate focused follow-up work if the work group wants to apply aliases across other semantically related but differently named parameters.
issue_request: FHIR-34866 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and asked to address inconsistent SearchParameter naming for equivalent authored-date usage, specifically authored, authored-on, and authoredon, by adding aliasCode support, naming guidance, examples, alias visibility, preferred-code identification, and compatibility aliases.
initial_application: The issue had been partially applied by commits 188ed0d92982a31f00ed9093844f90544b613a11 and 216f001194d17327f7b2ffdf9150b89b2303e5ae, merged through HL7/fhir#3967, which added SearchParameter.aliasCode plus naming guidance and examples. Those commits did not add aliases to the concrete DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, or Task authoredOn search parameters, so current source still lacked the consistent authored alternative for those legacy normative codes.
additional_context: DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, Task, and SearchParameter are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. The current SearchParameter notes document authored as the consistency example for authoring-date search parameters and aliasCode as the mechanism for backward-compatible renamed parameters. Because the affected primary codes are normative, the reconciliation preserved their published codes and added aliasCode instead of renaming them. FHIR-3855 and FHIR-25037 are related naming/alias precedents already represented on the combined branch and were not separate decisions here.
reconciliation: Added aliasCode="authored" to source/devicerequest/bundle-DeviceRequest-search-params.xml, source/medicationrequest/bundle-MedicationRequest-search-params.xml, and source/task/bundle-Task-search-params.xml. No broader preferred-code sweep was attempted because the Jira attachment inventory was not present in the prepared context and broader renames would need focused compatibility review.
